# Battery Cell Quality Statistical Case

[← Tesla](../README.md) · [Every Tesla question](../../tesla.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/battery-cell-quality-statistical-case)

`experiment-design` `probability`

---

## Study Requirements

- The batteries are divided into five groups.
- Assignment of batteries to groups is random.
- Every battery undergoes three distinct inspections or tests.
- Each inspection produces either a pass or a fail.
- The results have already been recorded.
- Identify the group with the strongest overall battery quality.

## Notes

- Approach this as an experimental-design and statistical-comparison problem rather than simply a SQL task.
- Establish the sample sizes, decide whether all three tests matter equally, assess whether failures are independent, and clarify whether a battery passes overall only when it passes every test.
- Suitable methods may include estimating group pass rates with confidence intervals, conducting hypothesis tests that account for multiple comparisons, and creating a combined quality score when test severities differ.
- When every battery has three binary results, specify the analysis unit before ordering the groups: the per-test pass rate, the rate of batteries passing all tests, and a weighted defect-severity score may identify different leaders.
- The question may depend on assumptions about the domain, so state those assumptions before selecting a statistical measure.

## Preparation

- Create a compact table containing `battery_id`, `group_id`, and three pass/fail fields; calculate each group’s size, pass rate for each test, all-tests-pass rate, and confidence intervals.
- Practice describing how random allocation is helpful while still requiring checks for group balance, absent inspections, and multiple testing across the five groups.
- Use a recommendation structure that ranks groups by the main quality measure, displays uncertainty ranges, identifies groups whose results cannot be meaningfully separated, and notes the additional data required before taking production action.
